3. In that suit defendant-petitioners filed an application under, Order VII, rule 11(d) read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure alleging that the predecessors of the defendant Nos. 1-3 had instituted the Other Class Suit No. 235 of 1972 before the then Munsif, Cox's Bazar impleading the predecessor of the defendant No. 4 and others as defendants for declaration of their title on the self-same land and for khas possession. The said suit was decreed on contest on 31-7-1986 and that the predecessor of the present defendant No. 4 and others had filed Other Appeal No. 144 of 1986 in the Court of learned District Judge who after hearing by judgment and decree dated 4-5-1987 allowed the appeal and thereby set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. Thereafter defendant-petitioners and their predecessor filed Civil Revision No. 562 of the 1987 before the High Court Division and upon contested hearing the Rule was made absolute and the Title Suit No. 235 of 1972 was decreed. The predecessor of the present plaintiff-opposite parties long after 6 years filed civil petition for Leave to Appeal No. 870 of 2009 before the Appellate Division who after hearing by judgment and order dated 12-11-2009 dismissed the civil Petition, thus the present suit is barred by principle of res-judicata. 

 7. Mr Dulal Mallick, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of defendant-petitioners has submitted that the predecessor of the present petitioners instituted Title Suit No. 235 of 1972 against the predecessor of the present plaintiff-opposite parties for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession and the said suit went upto the Appellate Division which affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court decreeing the suit and, as such, the present suit for the self-same suit land between the same parties are barred by the principle of res-judicata. He thereafter has submitted that from the judgment decree of the previous suit it would appear that predecessor of the present petitioners obtained decree declaring title and recovery of khas possession over the self-same property and thus, if the plaint cannot be rejected under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil procedure, the Court has ample power to reject the same under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure as the proceeding of the present suit will be a fruitless litigation. In support of his submission he referred the case of Abdul Jalil vs Islamic Bank Bangladesh Ltd reported in 53 DLR (AD) 12 and the case of Rasheda Begum vs MM Nurussafa reported in 24 BLD (AD) 223 = 9 BLC (AD) 223.
